"Game Development Request: Wild Boar Adventure

Create a complete, playable 3D third-person adventure game where the player controls a wild boar living in a forest.

IMPORTANT: Focus on creating a fully functional and polished game. Do not overcomplicate the project. Every requested feature must actually work. Prioritize gameplay, stability, and completeness over unnecessary complexity.

1. Main Character and Controls

- The player controls a wild boar.
- Use smooth third-person movement.
- Include walking, running, turning and attacking.
- Add simple and responsive camera controls.
- The boar should have basic animations whenever possible.

2. Forest Environment

- Create a beautiful, natural-looking forest.
- Add trees, bushes, rocks, grass and other environmental details.
- The forest should be large enough to explore but not unnecessarily huge.
- Add several small areas with different scenery.
- Keep the environment optimized for smooth performance.

3. Truffle Hunting

- Searching for truffles is one of the main gameplay activities.
- The boar can sniff and dig in specific locations.
- Truffles appear as collectible items.
- Different truffles have different values.
- Collecting truffles gives the player coins or points.
- Add a simple inventory or collection counter.

4. Combat and Enemies

- Add a few types of forest enemies, such as wolves and foxes.
- Enemies should have simple AI: patrol, detect the player, approach and attack.
- The boar can attack enemies using a head charge.
- Add a basic health system for the player and enemies.
- Defeating enemies gives rewards.
- Keep combat simple, responsive and enjoyable.

5. Simple Progression System

Include a small and understandable upgrade system.

The player can upgrade:

- Maximum health.
- Movement speed.
- Attack damage.

Use coins collected during gameplay to purchase upgrades.

Do not create complicated skill trees, dozens of statistics or complex progression mechanics.

6. Rewards and Achievements

- Add collectible coins and valuable truffles.
- Include a small achievement system.
- Examples: find 10 truffles, defeat 5 enemies, collect 100 coins.
- Display rewards clearly when achievements are unlocked.

7. User Interface

Create a clean, natural-looking interface that fits a forest adventure game.

Display:

- Player health.
- Coins.
- Collected truffles.
- Current objective.
- Upgrade menu.
- Pause menu.

Avoid futuristic designs, excessive neon colors and unnecessary visual effects.

8. Gameplay Objectives

Add a simple objective system:

- Find a certain number of truffles.
- Collect coins.
- Defeat a certain number of enemies.
- Unlock upgrades.

Give the player clear goals and rewards.

9. Audio

Add simple forest ambience, footsteps, digging sounds, animal sounds and combat effects where possible.

10. Language — Russian

The entire game must be in Russian from the very beginning.

- All menus and buttons must be in Russian.
- All objectives, quests and instructions must be in Russian.
- All achievements and notifications must be in Russian.
- All upgrade descriptions and interface elements must be in Russian.
- Do not leave any English text in the finished game.

11. Technical Requirements

- Create a complete and playable game, not just a prototype or visual demo.
- Use third-person 3D gameplay.
- Implement all core mechanics.
- Make sure all buttons and menus work.
- Ensure the game can be completed from start to finish.
- Avoid unnecessary complexity and features that could prevent successful compilation.
- Use simple, reliable systems instead of complicated mechanics.
- Test the game and fix errors before considering it finished.

FINAL PRIORITY:

A small but complete, enjoyable and polished wild boar adventure game is much better than a huge unfinished game. Focus on making the core gameplay work perfectly before adding optional content.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
